articles.title: The Worst GTA Game Is One Rockstar Could Never Make Today
articles.excerpt: GTA Advance might be one of the worst GTA games, but it was still an essential stepping stone for what makes GTA great today
articles.body: GTA Advance is an odd game. It's terrible in some ways, yet also not as bad as its reputation suggests. It's also an essential part of Rockstar history. This was Rockstar at a stage of uncertainty. The essence of the Grand Theft Auto franchise was still in flux, and the studio had yet to firmly decide on what, exactly, made a GTA game . GTA Advance has its strong points, but the most important thing about it is how it gave Rockstar (via developer Digital Eclipse) a chance to see where the series could fall short. It's a necessary bad game that paved the way for better ones — and the kind of essential failure the games industry can't tolerate anymore.

articles.body: Our time on our "space mission" underwater was coming to an end, and I felt like what I imagine an astronaut on the International Space Station (ISS) must feel before returning to Earth. On one hand, you are excited to return to your home and loved ones, as well as to fresh food and normal hygiene. On the other, you know you will miss your crew and the incredible experience of being in space. While my SEA STAR crew and I had not left Earth during our mission, we were separated from the surface of our home planet for five days. All we saw was a green alien water world surrounding us. We did this to live and work like astronauts on the ISS .

articles.excerpt: A badge that never expires is not a control. It is a spare key under the mat. On 27 October in Atlanta, IBM put a name on the agent and tied that name to a credential that is supposed to die. Keep tha…
articles.body: A badge that never expires is not a control. It is a spare key under the mat. On 27 October in Atlanta, IBM put a name on the agent and tied that name to a credential that is supposed to die. Keep that. Leave the kill switch in the keynote where it is. It is still a preview. Do not clap for a control you cannot press on a system that is already live. The secret is the stop Vault already does the useful thing for ordinary applications. It mints a secret for one job. Then the secret expires. Agent Identity, generally available today, is the row that secret has to match: who owns the agent, whether it is still allowed to work, and what it may touch. Step outside the row and Vault is built to refuse the call and end the session.

articles.title: What a Small RAG Fine-Tuning Experiment Can Actually Prove
articles.excerpt: I fine-tuned a pretrained reranker, verified that its weights changed, reloaded the selected checkpoint, and ran a controlled comparison with the original model. The measured ranking gain on the held-…
articles.body: I fine-tuned a pretrained reranker, verified that its weights changed, reloaded the selected checkpoint, and ran a controlled comparison with the original model. The measured ranking gain on the held-out synthetic slice was zero. That result was useful. It showed that the training and evaluation path executed while giving me no reason to claim an improvement. The slice contained three questions, only two of them answerable. Both rerankers reached nDCG@5 of 1.0 on those two answerable questions. This is a local, AI-assisted experiment in progress. Real-domain fine-tuning and a sealed real held-out comparison have not been completed. Human review of generated answers is also pending. The current evidence supports a working experimental pipeline and a tied result on a tiny synthetic fixture.

articles.title: Polling vs Webhooks for Crypto Payment Status: A Minimal Node.js Example
articles.excerpt: When you add crypto checkout to a store or SaaS app, the gateway confirms payments asynchronously. Blockchain confirmations take time, so your backend learns about a completed payment later, either be…
articles.body: When you add crypto checkout to a store or SaaS app, the gateway confirms payments asynchronously. Blockchain confirmations take time, so your backend learns about a completed payment later, either because the gateway calls you (webhook) or because you ask (polling). Most production setups use both. Here is why, with a minimal Express example. Webhooks: fast but not guaranteed A webhook arrives seconds after the gateway sees the payment reach the required confirmations. It is the fastest way to mark an order paid. But webhooks can be delayed, retried, delivered out of order or blocked by your firewall during a deploy. If your only signal is the webhook, a missed delivery means a paid customer with an unpaid order.

articles.body: Introdução Olá dando sequencia a minha série sobre IA para Devs. Hoje vamos entender como um LLM recebe um pedido, gera uma resposta e qual é seu papel em um agente de IA. Ah e se você perdeu o primeiro artigo ele foi sobre O que significa engenharia de prompt na prática? . Mas dando sequencia, vamos ao assunto de hoje. O que é? LLM é a sigla de Large Language Model (modelo de Linguagem de grande porte). É um modelo treinado para processar sequências de tokens e gerar respostas conforme a mensagem recebida. Muitos LLMs são modelos fundacionais (foundation models), treinados com grandes volumes de dados para realizar ou serem adaptados a diferentes tarefas. Também existem modelos fundacionais que trabalham com imagens, áudio e outros tipos de dados, são modelos multimodais.

articles.title: Checking hreflang Return Links Automatically With a Small Python Crawler
articles.excerpt: The most common hreflang bug is not a typo in a language code. It is a missing return link: page A says "my German version is B", but page B never points back to A. Search engines may then ignore the…
articles.body: The most common hreflang bug is not a typo in a language code. It is a missing return link: page A says "my German version is B", but page B never points back to A. Search engines may then ignore the pair. On a site with a few hundred localised pages this is tedious to check by hand, so here is a small script that does it. What we check For every page in a list of URLs: Fetch the HTML and read all <link rel="alternate" hreflang="..."> tags. For each alternate, fetch that URL and confirm it lists the original page back. Confirm each page includes a self-referencing hreflang entry. Flag alternates that return a non-200 status or redirect.

articles.title: Story points na prática: como estimar sem transformar em horas
articles.excerpt: Story points medem tamanho relativo (esforço, complexidade e incerteza), não horas. Neste texto eu explico a escala, por que Fibonacci funciona, como calibrar com uma história de referência e os erros…
articles.body: Story points medem tamanho relativo (esforço, complexidade e incerteza), não horas. Neste texto eu explico a escala, por que Fibonacci funciona, como calibrar com uma história de referência e os erros mais comuns. O que são story points Story points são uma unidade relativa de esforço. Eles resumem três coisas ao mesmo tempo: o trabalho necessário, a complexidade envolvida e a incerteza do que ainda não se sabe. Por serem relativos, pontos não têm valor absoluto. Uma história de 5 pontos não equivale a cinco horas nem a cinco dias: equivale a “mais ou menos isto” quando comparada com outras histórias do mesmo time. Também não são uma medida de produtividade individual.

articles.body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Someone has created a tool called UnknownAuto that lets self-built or sideloaded apps run on Android Auto. The tool marks the app as “installed from Google Play,” so Android Auto accepts it. UnknownAuto is billed as a free, open-source alternative to AA Enabler. Android Auto can run a large variety of apps, but not every app. The platform refuses to run apps that have been sideloaded. If there was ever an app you wished could run on Android Auto but doesn’t, there may be a solution. One user, who goes by u/mannumaster on Reddit, says they wanted to build their own app and use it on Android Auto. When they ran into roadblocks, they created a new tool called UnknownAuto.
